SQL:
WITH _base AS (
  SELECT
    customers.tier AS "customers.tier",
    COUNT(*) AS "customers._count",
    COUNT(DISTINCT customers.id) AS "customers.id_count_distinct"
  FROM customers AS customers
  GROUP BY
    customers.tier
), _cm_customers__orders__amount_sum AS (
  SELECT
    customers.tier AS "orders.customers.tier",
    CAST(SUM(orders.amount) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.amount_sum"
  FROM orders AS orders
  LEFT JOIN customers AS customers
    ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
  GROUP BY
    customers.tier
), _cm_customers__orders__id_count AS (
  SELECT
    customers.tier AS "orders.customers.tier",
    COUNT(orders.id) AS "orders.id_count"
  FROM orders AS orders
  LEFT JOIN customers AS customers
    ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
  GROUP BY
    customers.tier
)
SELECT
  _base."customers.tier",
  _base."customers._count",
  _base."customers.id_count_distinct",
  _cm_customers__orders__amount_sum."orders.amount_sum" AS "customers.orders.amount_sum",
  COALESCE(_cm_customers__orders__id_count."orders.id_count", 0) AS "customers.orders.id_count"
FROM _base
LEFT JOIN _cm_customers__orders__amount_sum
  ON _base."customers.tier" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM _cm_customers__orders__amount_sum."orders.customers.tier"
LEFT JOIN _cm_customers__orders__id_count
  ON _base."customers.tier" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM _cm_customers__orders__id_count."orders.customers.tier"
LIMIT 21

args.message: All 202 customers are included, grouped by tier. Revenue for each tier is the sum of order amounts across all orders of every status, including orders marked 'bad'. 6 orders belong to customer IDs that aren't in the customer table, so they have no tier and are left out. Customers with no orders count toward the tier's customer total but add nothing to its revenue.
